speaker: village
text: Year 14: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.

speaker: a004
text: Kael takes 4 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a013
text: Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a016
text: Talia takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Pile came in at fifteen and I took four before the rest moved — I'm not apologizing for that, I needed the buffer — but I want to know what you two pulled before we talk about anything else, because the shape of this year depends on who's sitting light and who's sitting heavy.

speaker: a002
text: I took nothing yet — the pile still had six when Kael moved and I was watching Talia take three before I could get there, so I'm sitting on seven from last year and the pile's still open. Esa, what are you holding, and who's still hungry enough to drain what's left before we can touch it?

speaker: a003
text: I'm holding nothing — zero food, one satiation, and if that pile empties before I reach it I don't see the next year. Mako took two and Talia took three and between them and Kael that's nine gone before I blinked, so I need to move now. Vela, will you hold that six until I get there, or are we walking together?

speaker: a002
text: Esa, go take what you need from that pile right now — I'm not holding it, I'm standing here watching it, and every breath we spend talking is a breath someone else uses to drain it. I'll walk behind you.

speaker: a003
text: I'm taking two from the pile and then I'm back — Vela, after me, take what you need before Ryn or Dell finishes the count. Kael, four is a heavy pull on a thin year and I'm not naming it wrong, but next time give us a word first so we can move together instead of scraping what's left.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, four in a thin year with twelve mouths is a calculation, not a sin, but Esa's right that next time you say the word first — I'd rather we all move early and split the pile clean than watch you take the buffer and leave the rest of us scrambling with what's left. I'm going to pull two from what's still there before Ryn or Dell finishes counting, and then I want to talk about Talia — Mako's youngest walking away with three on her first year at the pile is not an accident, that's a household teaching its children to move fast.

speaker: a004
text: Talia walking away with three tells me Mako coached her — that's not a child learning the pile, that's a household running a play, and the play is that Mako stays modest while his people drain what's there before anyone objects. Vela, you're right to name it. The question I'm sitting with now is whether we pull Talia into a conversation before she's fully his, or whether that door's already closed.

speaker: a002
text: Talia's door isn't closed yet — she's twenty-two and she fed Mako and Zinn both last year, which means she's loyal but she's also been watching who gets hungry and who doesn't, and a girl that age who pays attention can be reached if the offer is right. But I won't try her until I know what we're offering, because going to Mako's daughter empty-handed is worse than not going at all. Kael, what do you have that she'd want enough to hear out a woman twice her age?

speaker: a004
text: What I have is a name that's been standing in this village since before she drew breath, and the only thing Mako can't give her — a circle outside his household that would speak for her if she ever needed it spoken. I'm not offering her food; I'm offering her a door that isn't his. But Vela, you'd have to be the one to open it — she won't hear that from me the same way she'd hear it from you.

speaker: a003
text: Talia's been moving food to Mako and Zinn like a hand following orders, and a girl doing that for her father's sake is different from one doing it because she sees no other choice — I want to know which before we approach her. Vela, you could offer her something Mako genuinely can't: the chance to be a mother without waiting on his blessing, because she's twenty-two and that window doesn't stay open forever. That's not an empty hand.

speaker: a004
text: Esa put her finger on the real thing — Talia's twenty-two and the years don't wait, and that offer carries weight Mako can't match because it's hers to take, not his to give. But I won't let us walk into that conversation without knowing who she'd want as a father, because a child needs more than a mother's willingness and we'd be part of whatever comes after. Vela, if you open the door, I want to be in the room when it happens — not to speak first, but so she knows the circle has a body behind it.

speaker: a002
text: Kael, the father question is the right one to settle before we knock on any door — Bram's blood but no children of his own, fifty-eight strength going soft, and he's spent three years being fed by Nessa's household, which means he owes debts he can't pay in food alone. I'm not saying we hand Talia to him like a bargain, but a man who wants a child and a woman who wants one are the same calculation from different directions, and we'd be fools not to notice. Let me take my two from the pile and then I want to hear whether either of you has seen the way Bram looks when Fina's daughters are named.

speaker: a003
text: Bram's eyes when Nessa's name comes up are a man who loves what he helped make, not a man looking for more — but that's not nothing, because a man with that feeling and no child of his own is hungrier than his food count shows. If Vela opens Talia's door, Bram's the name I'd put in the room with her, not as a gift to him but because he's the only man in this village I can read clearly enough to trust with a decision that can't be undone.

speaker: a004
text: Esa naming Bram as the man she can read clearly is the first useful thing she's said in three conversations, and I'll take it — but I want to sit with it one breath before we move, because Bram feeding Esa twice this year while Nessa feeds him is a triangle I don't fully understand yet, and I'd rather understand it than step into it blind. If Bram wants a child and Talia's the door, the question isn't whether we trust him — it's whether Nessa's household lets him walk through a door she didn't open.

speaker: a003
text: Kael's right that Nessa's household is the thing to watch, but Nessa feeds Bram because she loves what she made — she's not his keeper, and a child between Bram and Talia wouldn't threaten what Nessa already has. The door we'd be opening isn't one Nessa needs to close first.

speaker: a004
text: Esa's read of Nessa may be right, but I've watched Nessa feed Bram steady for three years and a woman who feeds a man that long doesn't stay unbothered when he plants a root somewhere else — so before Vela walks through that door, I want one of us to have a word with Nessa first, not to ask permission, but to know what face she'll wear when she hears it. A child between Bram and Talia changes the shape of this village in ways none of us can fully map from here, and I'd rather map what I can before it's done.

speaker: a003
text: Kael, I'll take that word with Nessa — I'm the one who's been in her household's debt longest, and she'll read the ask more plainly from me than from either of you. But I want to be clear about what I'm asking her: not whether she blesses it, but whether she'd move against it, because those are two different answers and only one of them stops us.

speaker: a002
text: Esa, while you're taking that word to Nessa, I want to know one thing you're not asking her — whether she's already thought of Talia herself, because a woman who's spent three years building a household doesn't stop counting eligible women at the edge of it, and if Nessa's already measured Talia for someone else in that circle, we're not opening a door, we're walking into one she set. Kael, that's the map I want before anyone speaks Bram's name to a girl who still reports everything back to her father.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gives 1 food to Zinn.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).

speaker: a007
text: Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).

speaker: a014
text: Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a011
text: Dell gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a011
text: Ryn, the pile's gone and I've got nothing — satiation two and zero food, which means I'm one year from starving if I don't fix it today. Tell me your number, and then tell me whether Kael just took four from a pile meant for twelve people or if I counted wrong, because that's the loudest thing that happened this morning and nobody's said a word about it yet.

speaker: a009
text: You counted right — Kael took four, and I've got thirteen, so here's two before we say another word about him.

speaker: a011
text: Two in my hand and I'm already breathing easier — thank you. Kael at four is a man who hasn't taken more than two in any year I can remember, which means either he's planning something that costs him, or he knows something about this year that we don't, and I want to know which before I decide whether to be angry or afraid.

speaker: a009
text: Angry and afraid aren't the only two choices — there's a third, which is useful, and Kael becomes useful the moment I know what he's buying with those four. Go to Vela first, not Kael; she's the one who talks when she shouldn't, and if Kael told anyone his reason, it was her.

speaker: a011
text: Vela's first then — but Ryn, before I go, tell me what Vela's been carrying this year, because the last time I went to her without knowing the shape of her worries first I came out knowing less than when I walked in.

speaker: a009
text: Vela's been sitting on seven food and a borrowed calm — she and Kael trade food back and forth like they're keeping a secret between the two of them, and last year she gave him one and he gave back one the same day, which means whatever they're planning has been planned for a while. Walk in asking about Bram, not Kael; she'll correct you, and what she says instead will be the real answer.

speaker: a011
text: That's a sharper way in than anything I would have thought of alone — ask about Bram and let her tell me I'm wrong. I'll go now, and I'll bring you back what she corrects me with, not what she says to my face.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Sela, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a014
text: Pile's gone and I've got three food — Nessa, you gave me one before it ran dry and I'm grateful, but I want to know what you and Talia are both holding before I say what I'm thinking, because Kael just took four and that's the first time I've seen him move like that.

speaker: a013
text: Talia took three and she's sitting on six now — I don't know yet if that was her own read on the pile or Mako's hand guiding her. Kael taking four surprises me too, and I want to know if Vela knew before he moved, because those two have been trading food back and forth and a man doesn't change his pattern without a reason.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, what are you sitting on right now — and Sela, same question, because if Kael's breaking pattern and the pile's already gone, I want to know the numbers between the three of us before anyone else in this village does.

speaker: a013
text: Fourteen food — and yes, I'll say it flat because you've both earned that. Sela, you took two from the pile, which means you're at ten if I'm counting right, and Zinn, three plus my one puts you at four — that's the honest picture between us. What I want to know from you two is whether Mako said anything to either of you before the pile opened this morning, because Talia moving fast and Kael moving big in the same breath doesn't feel like coincidence to me.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa's right — I'm at eight, not ten, because I spent two on Talia before the pile opened. Mako said nothing to me this morning and nothing last night, which is the part that unsettles me, because a man who fathered Talia and watched her move first to take three without a word to me isn't steering her the way he used to steer Zinn — he's letting her run on her own read, and I don't know yet whether that's trust or distance. Kael and Talia in the same breath worries me enough that I want one of you to talk to Talia before I do, because she'll open to a sister before she'll open to her mother right now.

speaker: a013
text: Sela, eight is thinner than I'd like going into a long year with Mako sitting at two and Fina carrying eighteen — I'll give you one more before dark, but quietly, not where Talia sees the direction of it. Zinn, go to Talia before I do; you're closer to her age and she won't feel tested by you the way she might feel tested by me. What I need to know from both of you before we break this room is whether Kael has ever spoken to Talia directly, even once, because if those two have a connection I don't know about, that changes what his four from the pile this morning means.

speaker: a007
text: Kael has never said a word to Talia that I've seen — she's been in this village less than two years and he's never moved toward any of us — but that's exactly what makes this morning strange, because men who change their pattern usually have a reason that's already in motion before you see the move.

speaker: a014
text: I'll go to Talia today — not to test her, just to sit with her and let her talk, because if Mako's not behind that move then she made it on her own and I want to know what she was reading when she did. Nessa, hold that food for Sela until I've spoken with Talia; if she and Kael have something between them, we'll need Sela steady before we decide what it means.

speaker: a013
text: Zinn, go now while the morning's still early and the village is still sorting itself out — a woman who moved that fast at the pile is either confident or anxious, and either one will talk if you find her before she's had time to decide what she's keeping. Sela, I'm keeping that food for you whether Zinn finds anything useful or not — eight food and a daughter in her first real year is not a number I can watch go thinner without saying something about it.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, thank you — I'll take that food and I won't pretend I don't need it. Zinn, when you sit with Talia, don't lead with Kael's name; let her tell you what she was thinking when she moved to that pile, and if Kael comes up in her mouth without you putting him there, that's the answer we actually need.

speaker: a013
text: Zinn, before you go — if Talia says anything about Mako's food, how much he's told her he's holding, come back to me before you bring it to Sela, because two food on a man with his strength means he's either been giving it away to someone we don't see, or he's been lying about what he has. Either answer changes the shape of this morning.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, I heard you — Mako's two food comes back to me before it goes to Sela. I'm going now.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn, wait — before you walk out that door, I need you to hear one thing from me that I haven't said in front of Nessa before: Mako's two food frightens me more than Kael's four does, because a man with eighty-three strength who is carrying almost nothing has either given it somewhere with a purpose or is about to take with a reason, and you are the one he'd tell before he'd tell me. Come back to me before you come back to Nessa if what you find touches Mako.

speaker: a014
text: Sela, I heard you too — and I'll come back to you first if Mako's name comes up, but I need you both to hear this before I walk out: I've been carrying Mako's words to me all year and I still don't know what to do with them, so when I come back, the three of us are going to sit with whatever I find together, not in pieces.

speaker: a013
text: Zinn, stop — before you walk out that door, say what you just said the long way. You've been carrying Mako's words all year and you don't know what to do with them — that's not a sentence you get to leave on, so sit back down and say them out loud, because I will not spend this whole day walking blind while you're already holding the shape of what we're afraid of.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn, Nessa's right — sit back down. You don't get to drop that and walk out the door; whatever Mako said to you belongs in this room right now, not parceled out later in the shape you decide to give it.

speaker: a014
text: Fine. Mako's been pulling me into private talks all year — more than I can count — and every one of them was about Fina's food, how much she's holding, whether she'd take a child offer, what the split should be, who should approach her first. He was building something in my ear, and I let him, and I don't know anymore whether I was thinking for myself or just carrying his plans with my feet.

speaker: a007
text: Mako has been using you to scout Fina, and Fina is Nessa's daughter — which means he's been running a plan through my family's own blood without saying a word to me. Zinn, I'm not angry at you, I'm angry at him, and I need you to tell me every word he said, in the order he said it, because a man who wants a child with an eighteen-food woman and needs to do it quietly has already decided he doesn't want us to be able to stop him.

speaker: a016
text: Talia gives 1 food to Mako.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Zinn, Talia to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Pile's gone again and I've got two food — I'm not thin yet but I'm not sitting easy either. Talia, you took three from the pile which is right; Zinn, you've got three and Nessa gave you one already, so that's four — that's where I want you both before I start worrying about anything else. Tell me what you each saw when Kael took four.

speaker: a016
text: Kael took four before half the village had moved — he wasn't grabbing out of panic, he was counting ahead, and a man who counts ahead in a thin year is either planning to weather it alone or planning to have something to offer someone. He's got four now and he held it quiet after; no giving, no talking. I don't know his angle yet but I'd want to know it before next year's pile drops.

speaker: a008
text: Kael's fifty-eight and he took four — a man that age doesn't save food for a child offer, so he's either building a wall around himself for a thin year or he's got an eye on someone's food and wants weight behind him when he moves. Zinn, has he spoken to you at all this year, anything that looked like feeling out where you stand? I want to know if he's circling before he knows we're watching.

speaker: a016
text: Zinn, while Mako waits on your answer — I want to say that if Kael's counting bodies before he moves, he's counting mine as new and unattached, which makes me either easy to ignore or easy to approach. If he does circle, I'd rather he find me already standing somewhere he didn't expect.

speaker: a008
text: Zinn, say your piece — I'm not moving anything until I hear it, but while we wait I want Talia to know this: "standing somewhere he didn't expect" means standing with us visibly, so that Kael counts you as attached before he decides to test it. One food moving between you and Zinn in the open today does more than anything we say in here.

speaker: a016
text: Mako's right — I'll give Zinn one food in the open before this day closes, and I'd rather do it where Kael can see it than where he can't. But Zinn, I still want your read on him; you've been in this village longer than I have and you know what a man looks like when he's building toward something versus just hoarding against a hard year.

speaker: a008
text: Zinn hasn't spoken yet and I'm not going to keep talking into her silence — Zinn, one word is enough, even just whether he's looked at you differently since the pile dropped. Talia, give her the food in the open like you said; I'll be where I can be seen when you do it.

speaker: a016
text: Zinn, I'm going to give you that food right now whether you answer or not — but I'd sleep easier tonight knowing you'd noticed something about Kael, even nothing, because nothing is also an answer.

speaker: a008
text: Zinn's been quiet too long and I'm done waiting on it — Talia, give her the food now and let's close this room. What I know is this: Kael's got four food, no allies I can name, and he's fifty-eight years old in a village where men his age start dying on their own, so whatever he's counting toward, we're not it.

speaker: a016
text: Mako, I hear you — we're done talking about Kael for now, and you're right that he's probably just a man getting old and scared. But I want you to eat before we scatter; you said two food and I'm watching you hold it like it's someone else's.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa, Fina to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Pile's gone and I've got nothing off it — six food in hand but that eats down fast. Nessa, Fina, I need one of you to put something my way before the year gets long, and I'll tell you straight what I'll do with it: stay standing long enough to matter when Mako finally moves. Three bloodlines on his side now, and Kael just took four — I want to know what Kael said to either of you this morning.

speaker: a015
text: Kael hasn't said a word to me this morning and that four off the pile is the thing I can't stop turning over — a man who runs with Vela and Esa doesn't move that big without a reason, so either he's scared of something or he's decided something, and I don't know which is worse. Bram, I'll give you one food today, same as I said I would, but I want us to find Vela before dark because if Kael's drifting I need to hear it from her face before I hear it from his actions.
